description: Most-played Standard archetypes from the Magic.gg Metagame Mentor table of 2026-11-05 (Arena Championship 13 and Magic Spotlight: Fracture events, about 1,810 decklists). meta_share is the percentage of that field. See README.md in this folder for how the lists were gathered and their limits.

real_events.description: The events behind real_win_rate, for the Swiss comparison (python3 -m mtgsim calibrate; mtgsim/calibration.py): Arena Championship 13, 176 players, nine rounds of modified Swiss in which a player stops at 7 wins or 3 losses (magic.gg viewer's guide); Magic Spotlight: Fracture in Hartford (775 players) and Beijing (865), nine rounds, at most 3 losses to day two, fifteen rounds in all (melee.gg tournaments 440878 and 457663). Top 16 / top 8 playoffs left out. Checked 2026-11-23.

calibration: real_win_rate is the archetype's match win rate in the Magic.gg table of 2026-11-05 (checked against the article on 2026-11-14). sim_win_rate is its average win rate against the other seventeen decks in a 4,590-game mtgsim round robin (best-of-one, 30 games per pairing, seed 1, Forge AI on both sides, Forge commit 7db198d72e with mtgsim's fourteen Forge patches, combined hash e689217ab372, applied; measured 2026-11-17; 459 of its games replay identically with the revised patch 0020 of --mc deep, combined hash 69b5119ef601). sim_swiss_win_rate is its match win rate when that round robin's pairing results are played out as simulated Swiss events of the real events' structure (real_events; python3 -m mtgsim calibrate), the comparison to use because the real rates come from Swiss events. ai_pilot compares sim_swiss_win_rate with real_win_rate (since 2026-11-26; before, sim_win_rate): 'weak' means the AI does at least 10 points worse with the deck than people do, so beating it in a simulation says little; 'strong' means at least 10 points better; 'fair' is within 10 points.
